key_insight: Compressing a streaming geometry transformer's KV cache is not just a memory problem: different cache locations tolerate different levels of quantization, and compression errors can disrupt geometric predictions. QuantStream3D frames low-bit caching around preserving this geometric memory.
problem_solved: Historical key-value states help streaming models connect geometry across views, but their growing memory footprint limits long-sequence inference. Quantizing these states can distort retrieval and affect downstream geometry estimation.
method: Systematically characterize KV-cache quantization in streaming visual geometry transformers.
Identify nonuniform geometric sensitivity across precision choices and cache locations.

Examine cache-geometry mismatch: perturbed retrieval changes geometry-head inputs, motivating geometry-aligned low-bit caching. The supplied abstract is truncated, so implementation details are unavailable.
impact: This work highlights why low-bit cache compression for geometry models should account for downstream geometric accuracy, not just memory savings. It could guide more memory-efficient long-sequence inference, although the supplied excerpt provides no quantitative results.

paper_title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
paper_authors: Zunhai Su, Keyu Fan, Ruishan Guo, Zhongzhu Zhou, Jingzehua Xu
